Subject: MAP + success criteria for pilot evaluation

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for the demo last week. We want to move quickly to a short evaluation (4 weeks) to validate Redwood for our portal chat and triage flows. Procurement asked I put together a list of what we need to see to consider this a success. High level asks:

- Proof of 99th percentile latency under typical traffic (target: <= 300ms per token)
- Cost estimate per 1,000 users per month (ballpark)
- Evidence of data isolation (how logs/inputs are stored in Hosted vs Dedicated)
- A short set of acceptance tests we can run against real traffic samples

Can you send a MAP and a proposed acceptance checklist we can use to sign off at the end of the pilot? Procurement loops: procurement@medpro.com.

Appreciate a draft by Monday so we can review with engineering and procurement next week.

Best,
Samantha

MedPro Solutions

Hi Samantha —

Thanks — attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan and an evaluation rubric (MAP-draft-v1.xlsx, evaluation-rubric-v2.pdf). Key points at a glance:

1) Timeline (4 weeks)
   - Week 0: kickoff + data handoff (we'll provision a sandbox instance)
   - Week 1: smoke tests + latency baseline
   - Week 2: real-traffic integration (masked samples)
   - Week 3: canary/operational run & concordance checks
   - Week 4: acceptance window and official sign-off

2) Exit gates / acceptance tests
   - Latency: 99th percentile token generation <= 350ms in sandbox; <= 300ms target in dedicated run (measured over 95% of traffic slices)
   - Accuracy: top-1 task routing precision >= 92% on your labeled sample set
   - Cost: projected token spend per 1,000 monthly active users within 25% of the provided estimate
   - Reliability: automatic fallback to smaller model on failure with <0.5% request drop

3) Evidence / artifacts for sign-off
   - Latency logs (token-level breakdown), cost runbook, model config snapshot, sample conversation concordance report, and runbook for rollback triggers.

4) Who does what (mutual action items)
   - MedPro: provide masked traffic sample + label set, evaluate the rubric items, and confirm procurement requirements
   - Redwood (Priyom): deliver sandbox, run tests, provide logs and acceptance artifacts
   - Redwood (Karthik): onboard model, tune batching/quantization, run perf tests

Next steps: can we lock a 30-45 minute cadence for the weeks 0–2 technical syncs? Proposed: Mon/Wed 11am PT.

I've included short attachment stubs and a link to the shared MAP folder. If anything looks off I can revise the rubric before Monday review.

Thanks —
Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.xlsx, evaluation-rubric-v2.pdf

Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP + success criteria for pilot evaluation

Agree with Priyom's draft — adding the technical acceptance test checklist I will own:

- Throughput / latency profile: run 10-minute sustained window at expected concurrency and capture p50/p90/p99 for token generation and end-to-end response time. Provide the raw KV cache hit ratio.
- Tokenization compatibility: verify tokenizer match for training/production; reject samples that change token counts by >10%
- Stability: perform a rolling restart test (20% of nodes) with no >2% error rate increase
- Concordance harness: run 1,000 labeled queries through the pipeline; produce confusion matrix + example cases for review

Also: we'll include a recommended canary rollout policy in the MAP: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback on latency or error rate breach. I'll attach a short perf-run script and the exact metric names we will surface in the console.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Samantha —

Great notes. Confirmations below and next steps: 

- SLA during pilot: Redwood will provide an operational SLO of 99.5% availability for the dedicated sandbox endpoints used in the evaluation window. We will surface uptime and incident logs in the shared console.
- Data handling: masked traffic provided by MedPro will not be used for model training, fine-tuning, or benchmarking without explicit, written agreement. Redwood will retain logs only for the duration of the pilot (30 days post-run) unless you request extended retention; all logs in the sandbox are encrypted and access-controlled.
- Latency gate: we'll make the acceptance target p99 <= 300ms for the final acceptance run on the dedicated environment; sandbox baseline will remain p99 <= 350ms during early weeks. Karthik has agreed to run perf tuning during Week 1–2 to narrow the gap.

Final action items to close the MAP:
1) MedPro: confirm masked sample handoff and availability for the Week 2 canary (target date: 2026-12-01).
2) MedPro procurement: send DOCuSign PO template or any required compliance attachments by 2026-11-24.
3) Redwood: finalize the MAP document (I will upload v1.1 with the slight wording changes and add the SLO table).

I'll upload MAP-draft-v1.1 to the shared Drive and send the calendar invite for Mon 11/23 10:00am PT. If that works we'll treat that call as the formal kickoff.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the line.

Priyom Das
